samples.summary: The `/^data:/i` case-insensitivity fix has no test
samples.evidence: `imageInline` was changed from `image.src.startsWith('data:')` to `/^data:/i.test(image.src)`, and its comment names the exact bug it fixes ("Spelled `DATA:` this test used to answer `false`, so a data URL was emitted inline with `inlineImages` off"). Grepping `packages/docs/test/serialize/markdown.test.ts` for `DATA:` / any uppercase-scheme data URI returns nothing: every data-URI test uses lowercase `data:image/png;base64,AAAA` (lines 343, 361, 669, 724, 793), which passes with or without the `i` flag. Note `SAFE_IMAGE_DATA_URI` is already case-insensitive, so an uppercase `DATA:image/png;base64,…` still passes the safety gate — the only thing distinguishing old from new behaviour is the `inlineImages:false` placeholder branch, and nothing exercises it.

samples.summary: `sectPrLengthPx`'s `allowZero` distinction (a 0 margin is legitimate, a 0 page size is not) is only half tested
samples.evidence: The new helper's docstring says the whole point of `allowZero` is that "a margin of 0 is a legitimate edge-to-edge layout" while a 0 page dimension is broken. The new tests in packages/docs/test/import/docx-parser.test.ts cover `<w:pgSz w:w="0">` → default (line 187) and non-numeric/negative margins → default (lines 195-201), but no case asserts `<w:pgMar w:top="0" …>` yields margin 0 rather than falling back to 96. If `allowZero` were inverted or ignored for margins, every listed test would still pass while imported edge-to-edge documents silently gained 1" margins.

samples.summary: Test comment claims "nothing was pushed onto the undo stack on the way to the refusal" but asserts no such thing
samples.evidence: In the `refuses %s, and writes nothing` case the comment states the refusal leaves the undo stack untouched, yet the only assertions are `editor.getPageSetup()` equals the default and `store.getDocument().pageSetup` is undefined. Neither can distinguish "assert before snapshot" from "snapshot then assert" — a stray empty undo entry (a user pressing Ctrl+Z and seeing nothing happen) would pass. No `undo()` call or snapshot spy appears anywhere in this file.

samples.summary: "a page-setup change is one undo step" cannot detect a double snapshot
samples.evidence: The test writes a setup then calls `editor.undo()` once and asserts the setup equals `DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP`. If `writePageSetup` took two snapshots, both would capture the same pre-write state, so a single undo would still restore the default and the test would pass. The format-painter suite in editor-format-painter.test.ts explicitly solves this by making a distinguishable prior edit as an undo-stack floor and undoing twice; this test does not.
searchedFor: read editor-page-setup.test.ts 'a page-setup change is one undo step'
compare with editor-format-painter.test.ts 'a paste is one undo step'

samples.summary: `fitMargins`' proportional-shrink behaviour is untested — only positivity is asserted
samples.evidence: `fitMargins` documents that it shrinks a margin pair *proportionally* "so a document whose margins are merely too large for its page keeps the ratio its author chose". Both new tests that hit this path (types.test.ts 'leaves a positive content box when margins would close it', with equal 5000/5000 margins, and docx-parser.test.ts 'leaves a positive content box when the margins swallow the page', also symmetric) assert only `> 0`. A reset-to-default or a set-both-to-zero implementation would pass both. No test uses an asymmetric over-large pair (e.g. left 900 / right 300) and checks the ratio survives.
searchedFor: grep for asymmetric margin fixtures in types.test.ts / docx-parser.test.ts

samples.evidence:
`LINE_SEPARATORS = /[

samples.evidence: The rewritten resolver added `orientation = resolved.orientation === 'landscape' ? 'landscape' : 'portrait'`, which coerces a garbage/undefined orientation from a CRDT write. The new tests in types.test.ts cover a landscape setup and a `{}` setup, but none passes an invalid orientation value (e.g. `'sideways'` or `undefined` alongside a valid paperSize) and asserts it comes back as `'portrait'`.

The new `EditorAPI.pasteFormat` wrapper calls `notifyStyleApplied()` only when the paste reported a write, with a comment that the toolbar pickers re-read their summaries off `onCursorMove`. editor-format-painter.test.ts asserts the style landed and the return value, but never subscribes to `onCursorMove` to check the notification fires (and does not fire on a no-op paste). A regression here would leave the toolbar showing stale formatting after a paint — visible to users, silent to the suite.

samples.summary: `formatSourcePosition`'s final fallback branch (no selected block carries text) is untested
samples.evidence: After the forward walk, the function falls back to `{ blockId: normalized.start.blockId, offset: normalized.start.offset }` for a selection where nothing selected holds text. The new tests in editor-format-painter.test.ts cover the caret case, the backward selection, the block-end walk-forward and the table rectangle, but none constructs a selection spanning only empty blocks, so this branch never executes.
